1#main: That one should not inflict a blemish on a firstborn. In it are 7 seifim. It is forbidden to inflict a blemish on a firstborn, even to cause a blemish indirectly—such as placing a fig on its ear so a dog takes it from there and cuts its ear with it, and the like; or telling a gentile to inflict a blemish on it. And if he made a blemish with his hands or through his causation, they do not slaughter it based on him until another blemish befalls it on its own. And if it died, they do not fine him; rather they slaughter it based on him.
2#main: If a gentile or a minor inflicted a blemish on it on its own—if he did not intend to permit it, it is permitted, even if he asked why they do not slaughter it and they answered him offhand that it is forbidden to slaughter until a blemish befalls it; but if he intended to permit it, such as after he sees they permit through this he does so for others—it is forbidden. (If there is doubt whether he intended to permit or not, we follow the lenient view (Hagahos Mordechai, Chullin). And if a gentile speaks offhand and says the Israelite commanded him—it is forbidden (Terumat HaDeshen siman 169).)
3#main: If they told a gentile maidservant serving in a Jewish house about the firstborn that it is not eaten without a blemish, and she went and cut its ear—it is considered intentional and they do not slaughter based on her, because this gentile maidservant intended to permit it; and also those who told her it is not eaten without a blemish intended that she inflict a blemish on it. {Rama: It is permitted to give a firstborn to a gentile to raise it, and if the guardian inflicted a blemish on it, it is permitted, and we do not say he intended to permit it—even though he knows it is permitted through its blemish and that it is a firstborn (Piskei Maharai siman 168).}
4#main: If the firstborn was pursuing him and he kicked it and through that made a blemish in it—it is permitted to slaughter based on it, even if it kicked him after he was saved from it.
5#main: By Torah law, a firstborn in which a transient blemish befell—it is permitted to inflict a permanent blemish on it; but the Sages forbade it.
6#main: A firstborn seized by blood—one may let blood, provided he does not intend to make a blemish; and if a blemish was made through this letting of blood, behold it may be slaughtered based on it.
7#main: It is permitted to inflict a blemish on a firstborn at this time before it comes into the air of the world.
